Formulation
- Predisposing factors: history of hypothyroidism.
- Precipitating factors: change of workplace to new law firm ~3–3.5 months ago concurrent with onset of low mood and reduced appetite.
- Perpetuating factors: stopped taking thyroxine and no recent blood tests; reduced physical activity; ongoing symptoms (fatigue, nausea, palpitations) impacting intake and energy.
- Protective factors: employed, partnered, help-seeking behavior.
- Summary: A 35-year-old (age stated) patient reports months of low mood, low energy, decreased appetite with ~1 stone weight loss over ~6 months, situational palpitations/shortness of breath and nausea. He has a history of hypothyroidism but reports stopping thyroxine since changing doctors. Plan focused on medical re-evaluation (blood tests) to identify reversible contributors and follow-up for further assessment and management.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Low mood / depressive symptoms
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Improve mood, increase energy and appetite, and reduce functional impact at home and work.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Exclude or identify medical contributors to low mood (e.g., anemia, metabolic, hepatic, renal, vitamin deficiencies, thyroid dysfunction); formulate further psychiatric/psychological management after results.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Call support via the app (telephone number provided in app) to arrange blood tests as discussed.
  - Attend arranged blood tests.
  - Contact service promptly if symptoms significantly worsen.
  - Seek urgent care/A&E if develops chest pain or severe new symptoms.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Arrange "general set of bloods" as discussed (to assess anemia, renal function, liver function, vitamin levels — as stated); clinician to provide blood test form.
  - Review results and arrange physical examination if bloods are normal.
  - Provide advice to seek emergency care (A&E) for chest pain or acute deterioration.
  - Send text to patient with instructions to book follow-up appointment after blood test results.

Secondary Problem: Anxiety symptoms / palpitations and situational shortness of breath
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce frequency/intensity of palpitations and breathlessness episodes; improve ability to tolerate lifts/trigger situations.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Determine medical vs anxiety-related cause of palpitations and breathlessness; manage accordingly.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Note circumstances/timing of palpitations and report these during follow-up.
  - Attend for any recommended investigations or examinations.
  - Seek immediate care for chest pain or new concerning symptoms.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Include investigation of possible medical causes in blood tests and consider further cardiac/physical assessment if indicated after initial results.
  - Proceed to physical examination or refer for urgent assessment only if clinical findings warrant; advise A&E if chest pain occurs.

Tertiary Problem: Untreated/under-investigated hypothyroidism (thyroxine non-adherence)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Re-establish appropriate monitoring and management of thyroid condition.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Check thyroid function and consider resumption/titration of thyroxine based on results and clinical review.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Arrange and attend blood tests; inform clinician of prior thyroxine use and that medication was stopped.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Include thyroid function testing as part of investigations (implied in general bloods) and interpret in context of symptoms; advise on medication restart/titration after results and clinical review.

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered:
  - Need for blood tests to evaluate anemia, kidney/liver function, vitamin levels and to clarify medical contributors to symptoms.
  - Importance of seeking urgent care/A&E for chest pain or acute deterioration.
  - How to contact the service/support via the app (phone number) to arrange investigations.
  - To re-contact service if bowel symptoms change or if vomiting/other new symptoms develop.
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - New or worsening chest pain; change in bowel habits, vomiting; significant functional decline; marked worsening of mood or suicidal thoughts (patient instructed to contact services/seek emergency care).
- Coping Strategies:
  - Contact service/support and attend investigations; seek help promptly for worsening symptoms. (No specific psychological coping strategies were recorded in the consultation.)

Quality checks
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Formal psychiatric diagnosis, suicide risk level, complete MSE (appearance/orientation/memory), detailed medication doses, allergy status, smoking/alcohol/substance use history, explicit referral to mental health services or psychosocial interventions.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Timeline of weight loss/onset: patient variably described symptom onset as ~3–3.5 months since job change vs weight loss starting earlier (~6 months) — conflict noted.
  - Thyroid symptom picture vs reported history: patient reports underactive thyroid and stopping thyroxine; clinician noted some symptoms (palpitations) are more typical of overactive thyroid — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality notes:
  - Several short pauses and inaudible/missing segments; some patient responses were fragmented. Some clinical details (exact DOB, contact details, GP details, medication dose) were not provided in the transcript.
